title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from this page and the neighbouring context). A is a Dedekind-type base ring. E is a (central) simple algebra. O is an order in E, probably a maximal one, and C is an A-linear category of 'lattices'. For an object X of C, O = End(X), and C is Morita-equivalent to O-modules. Taking the object X gives a functor α_X from the Gr-category (categorical group, Picard groupoid) Eq(C,C) of autoequivalences of C to the Gr-category of 'special (O,O)-réseaux'. These are invertible two-sided O-lattices L ⊂ E, i.e. invertible O-bimodules together with an embedding into E. Composition corresponds to the product LM.

The constraint. The page first notes that the identification LM = ML inside E gives a commutativity constraint c_X : LM ≅ ML. This is legitimate if two-sided invertible ideals of the order commute, as they do for maximal orders. It is independent of the chosen embeddings L→E, M→E, since these are unique up to central scalars, which do not affect the equality LM = ML.

Proposition. The constraint transported to Eq(C,C) does not depend on the choice of X.

An abandoned bracketed remark says invariance under replacing X by an isomorphic object is clear. It adds that one 'should' give a small general argument. In a Gr-category B, one would have to see which autoequivalences, such as conjugation by an object, preserve a commutativity constraint, strict or not. This is left unfinished.

Proof. Let X' be another choice, given by a projective P ∈ ℙ(O'/A); one may take P ⊂ E. Then O' = End_O(P) = {λ ∈ E : λP ⊂ P} is embedded in E, and P is an (O',O)-réseau (an invertible bimodule, i.e. a Morita equivalence). A lemma gives a commutative triangle: α_{X'} ≅ (L ↦ P L P^{-1}) ∘ α_X. So it suffices to check that conjugation by P carries c_X to c_{X'}. This holds because P(LM)P^{-1} = (PLP^{-1})(PMP^{-1}) and P(ML)P^{-1} = (PMP^{-1})(PLP^{-1}), using P^{-1}P = O. Since c_X = 1, i.e. the equality LM = ML in E, its transport is the equality inside E, which is c_{X'} = 1. 'OK.'

Purpose. This puts a canonical symmetric (strictly commutative) structure on the Picard 2-group of autoequivalences of a Morita class of maximal orders. In the context of the 'Galois theory of motives' notes, it plausibly serves the computation of bands (liens) and automorphism groups of fibre functors for lattice-valued or arithmetic tannakian situations.
errors: Commutativity LM = ML of invertible two-sided lattices is assumed without proof. It holds for maximal orders (and for 'special' ones if so defined), but not for arbitrary orders; the hypothesis is implicit.
The general statement about autoequivalences of a Gr-category preserving a commutativity constraint is explicitly left unproved ('Il faudrait une petite démonstration').
The lemma giving the commutative triangle α_{X'} ≅ conj_P ∘ α_X is stated, not proved; it is standard Morita theory.

ideas.what: Gr-category of autoequivalences of a linear category identified, via a generator X, with invertible O-bimodules embedded in E
ideas.modern_name: Picard 2-group / Morita theory (Pic of an order)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Morita, Bass; Fröhlich for orders (1973); Hoàng Xuân Sính for Gr-catégories
ideas.where_published: Gr-catégorie terminology appears in Sính's thesis, written under Grothendieck

ideas.what: Commutativity constraint on that Picard category given by LM = ML in E, independent of the embeddings
ideas.modern_name: symmetric (strictly commutative) Picard category structure on Pic of a maximal order
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; commutativity of two-sided ideals of maximal orders is classical (Deuring, Reiner)

ideas.what: Independence of the constraint from the choice of generator, via conjugation by an invertible bimodule P

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags a general question left unworked: characterising which autoequivalences of a Gr-category (e.g. conjugations) preserve a given commutativity constraint, strict or not. This is a question about how the braiding interacts with the action of the 2-group on itself, later handled in braided/symmetric 2-group theory.
missed.quote: Il faudrait une petite démonstration : dans une Gr-catégorie B, les autoéquivalences qui transforment une contrainte de comm. (stricte ou non) en elle-même ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: an early instance of the braided 2-group viewpoint applied to arithmetic Picard groups of orders, but the content is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine but early, careful check that a symmetric structure on the Picard 2-group of a maximal order is Morita-invariant. It uses Gr-category language before its published appearance (Sính 1975), but the mathematics is standard.
transcription_corrections: 'viscaux' / 'viscam' / 'bivisca' is very likely 'réseaux' / 'réseau' / 'biréseau' (lattices): 'Catégorie des (O,O)-réseaux spéciaux', 'P est un (O',O)-réseau'.
'E_X (C,C)' at the top of the diagram is likely 'Eq(C,C)' (category of autoequivalences of C), with α_X : Eq(C,C) → (O,O)-réseaux spéciaux.
First line probably: 'Il est immédiat que ceci ne dépend pas des choix des plongements L→E, M→E' rather than 'donne un diagramme bien des choix'.
'O' = End_O(P)' and 'c'est l'ensemble des λ ∈ E tels que λP ⊂ P' are confirmed by the image.
